subject: math
title: Grade 7 Adding and Subtracting Integers
seo_title: Grade 7 Adding and Subtracting Integers Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Use objects, diagrams, and equations to represent, describe, and solve situations involving addition and subtraction of integers
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 math worksheets on adding and subtracting integers for the Ontario curriculum: integer tiles and zero pairs, number lines, adding integers, subtracting by adding the opposite, and word problems with temperatures, elevations and bank balances. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: To subtract an integer, add its opposite: 5 − (−3) = 5 + 3 = 8.
key_sub: Same signs: add and keep the sign, so −6 + (−5) = −11. Different signs: subtract and use the sign of the number farther from 0, so −3 + 5 = 2, not −8.
body_html:
Zero pairs

A yellow tile is +1 and a red tile is −1. One yellow tile and one red tile make a zero pair: 1 + (−1) = 0. You can add or remove zero pairs without changing the value.

Adding on a number line

Start at the first number. Adding a positive number moves right. Adding a negative number moves left.

Rules for adding

SignsWhat to doExample
Same signsAdd the sizes. Keep the sign.−6 + (−5) = −11
Different signsSubtract the sizes. Use the sign of the number farther from 0.−3 + 5 = 2
Example 1

What is 8 + (−13)?

Different signs: 13 − 8 = 5. −13 is farther from 0, so the answer is negative.

Answer: −5

Subtracting: add the opposite

To subtract an integer, add its opposite. Keep the first number, change − to +, and change the sign of the second number.

Example 2

What is −6 − 4?

Add the opposite: −6 + (−4). Same signs: 6 + 4 = 10, keep the negative sign.

Answer: −10

Example 3

At 6 a.m. in Thunder Bay it was −16 °C. At 2 p.m. it was 2 °C. How many degrees did the temperature rise?

Later − earlier: 2 − (−16) = 2 + 16 = 18.

Answer: 18 degrees

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
−3 + 5 = −8Different signs: subtract the sizes. −3 + 5 = 2
5 − (−3) = 2Add the opposite: 5 + 3 = 8
4 + (−9) = 5Use the sign of the number farther from 0: −5
−6 + (−2) = 8Same signs keep the sign: −8
Counting the starting point as a hopCount the jumps, not the dots

faq.q: How do you add and subtract integers in Grade 7?
faq.a: To add, look at the signs: with the same signs, add and keep the sign; with different signs, subtract and use the sign of the number farther from 0. To subtract, add the opposite: 5 − (−3) = 5 + 3 = 8.

faq.q: Which Ontario Grade 7 expectation covers adding and subtracting integers?
faq.a: Expectation B2.4 in the Number strand of the 2020 Ontario math curriculum: students use objects, diagrams and equations to add and subtract integers in real situations.

faq.q: What is a zero pair in math?
faq.a: A zero pair is one positive tile and one negative tile, because +1 + (−1) = 0. Removing zero pairs does not change the value, so −7 + 3 leaves 4 red tiles, which is −4.

faq.q: Why does subtracting a negative number make the answer bigger?
faq.a: Subtracting is the same as adding the opposite, so 5 − (−3) = 5 + 3 = 8. On a number line, 5 is 8 steps to the right of −3.

items.e: Each yellow and red pair is a zero pair: 1 + (−1) = 0. There are 2 zero pairs. Remove them: 4 yellow tiles are left. The tiles show 4.

items.e: The first group has 7 yellow tiles, so it is 7. The second group has 3 red tiles, so it is −3. The tiles show 7 + (−3).

items.q: Mateo models −7 + 3 with tiles. What is the sum?
items.e: Make 3 zero pairs and remove them. 4 red tiles are left. Different signs: subtract the sizes, 7 − 3 = 4. −7 is farther from 0, so the answer is negative. −7 + 3 = −4.

items.q: Arjun models 4 + (−9) with tiles. What is the sum?
items.e: Make 4 zero pairs and remove them. 5 red tiles are left. Different signs: subtract the sizes, 9 − 4 = 5. −9 is farther from 0, so the answer is negative. 4 + (−9) = −5.

items.q: Priya models −2 + (−5) with tiles. What is the sum?
items.e: All the tiles are red, so there are no zero pairs. Count them: 7 red tiles. −2 + (−5) = −7.

items.q: Emma models 8 + (−3) with tiles. What is the sum?
items.e: Make 3 zero pairs and remove them. 5 yellow tiles are left. Different signs: subtract the sizes, 8 − 3 = 5. 8 is farther from 0, so the answer is positive. 8 + (−3) = 5.

items.q: Owen models −6 + 6 with tiles. What is the sum?
items.e: Make 6 zero pairs and remove them. No tiles are left, so the sum is 0. A number plus its opposite is always 0.

items.q: Chloe wants to show −2 with integer tiles. She starts with 6 red tiles. How many yellow tiles does she need to add?
items.e: The 6 red tiles show −6. Each yellow tile you add makes a zero pair with a red tile and raises the value by 1. To get to −2, add 4 yellow tiles: −6 + 4 = −2.

items.q: Nathan shows an integer with 3 yellow tiles and 11 red tiles. What integer is it?
items.e: 3 zero pairs are worth 0. The other 8 red tiles are worth −8. So 3 yellow tiles and 11 red tiles show 3 + (−11) = −8.

It is negative, because −53 is farther from 0.
items.e: The signs are different, so the sum has the sign of the number farther from 0. 53 > 38, so the sum is negative (it is −15).

sets.title: Word problems: temperatures, elevations and money

items.q: At 7 a.m. on a January day in Thunder Bay, the temperature was −21 °C. By noon it had risen 13 degrees. What was the temperature at noon?
items.e: Rising means adding: −21 + 13 = −8 °C.

items.q: In Sudbury, it was 5 °C at 5 p.m. The temperature fell 11 degrees by midnight. What was the temperature at midnight?
items.e: Falling means subtracting: 5 − 11 = 5 + (−11) = −6 °C.

items.q: On the same winter morning, it was 4 °C in Toronto and −17 °C in Thunder Bay. How many degrees warmer was Toronto?
items.e: Find the difference: 4 − (−17) = 4 + 17 = 21 degrees. On a number line, 4 to 0 is 4 and 0 to −17 is 17: 4 + 17 = 21.

items.q: At the bottom of a ski hill near Collingwood, the temperature is −5 °C. At the top it is 3 degrees colder. What is the temperature at the top?
items.e: Colder means subtracting: −5 − 3 = −5 + (−3) = −8 °C.

items.q: In Thunder Bay, the temperature was −14 °C at 7 a.m. and 3 °C at 3 p.m. How many degrees did the temperature rise?
items.e: Rise = later temperature − earlier temperature: 3 − (−14) = 3 + 14 = 17 degrees.

items.q: A bakery in Hamilton had a loss of $12 500 in its first year, written as −$12 500. It had a profit of $18 200 in its second year. What is the total for the two years?
items.e: Add the two results: −12 500 + 18 200 = $5700. The profit is farther from 0, so the total is positive.

items.q: Ethan is scuba diving near Tobermory at −15 m. He swims up 6 m. What is his new position?
items.e: Up means adding: −15 + 6 = −9 m. He is still below the surface.

items.q: Leah is diving at −10 m in Lake Huron. She goes down another 8 m to look at a shipwreck. What is her new position?
items.e: Down means subtracting: −10 − 8 = −10 + (−8) = −18 m.

items.q: Mei is diving at −7 m and Lucas is diving at −19 m. How far apart are they?
items.e: Subtract the positions: −7 − (−19) = −7 + 19 = 12 m. Both are below the surface, so the distance is 19 − 7.

items.q: The CN Tower in Toronto is 553 m tall. Ground level is 0 m, and a subway tunnel nearby is at −20 m. How much higher is the top of the CN Tower than the tunnel?
items.e: 553 − (−20) = 553 + 20 = 573 m. Count 20 m up to ground level, then 553 m more.

items.q: The surface of Lake Superior is about 183 m above sea level. Its deepest point is 406 m below the surface. What is the elevation of the deepest point compared with sea level?
items.e: Start at 183 and go down 406: 183 − 406 = 183 + (−406) = −223 m. The deepest point is below sea level.

items.q: Liam has $35 in his bank account. He buys a $50 video game with his debit card, and the account goes below zero. What is the balance now?
items.e: Spending means subtracting: 35 − 50 = 35 + (−50) = −$15. He owes the bank $15.

items.q: Benjamin’s bank balance is −$25. He deposits $60 of birthday money. What is the balance now?
items.e: A deposit means adding: −25 + 60 = $35.

items.q: Ava’s balance is −$18. She deposits $30, then spends $20 at a sports store in Ottawa. What is the balance now?
In a Toronto parkade, the ground floor is level 0 and the levels below it are −1, −2, and so on. Sofia parks on level −5 and takes the elevator up to level 2. How many levels does she go up?
items.e: 2 − (−5) = 2 + 5 = 7 levels. Count 5 levels up to 0, then 2 more.

items.q: Jayden gets on the elevator in a Mississauga building on level 6. He goes down 9 levels to the parkade. Which level is he on now?
items.e: Down means subtracting: 6 − 9 = 6 + (−9) = −3.

items.q: In a class quiz game, a right answer is +10 points and a wrong answer is −15 points. A team has −25 points and then gets one wrong answer. What is the team’s score now?
items.e: A wrong answer adds −15: −25 + (−15) = −40.

items.q: In hockey, a player’s plus-minus goes up 1 when the player’s team scores while the player is on the ice, and down 1 when the other team scores. Aiden’s plus-minus is 2. In the next game, his team scores 1 goal and the other team scores 4 while he is on the ice. What is his plus-minus now?
items.e: The change is 1 + (−4) = −3. Then 2 + (−3) = −1.

items.q: In Thunder Bay, the temperature dropped 14 degrees overnight. In the morning it was −22 °C. What was the temperature the evening before?
items.e: Work backwards: the evening was 14 degrees warmer. −22 + 14 = −8 °C.

items.q: In one week in Thunder Bay, the highest temperature was 6 °C and the lowest was −27 °C. What is the difference between the highest and lowest temperatures?
items.e: 6 − (−27) = 6 + 27 = 33 degrees. From −27 up to 0 is 27 degrees, and 0 up to 6 is 6 more.
